2607.22725.title: Structural Preservation Governs Data Augmentation in Deep Learning-Based Laser Speckle Material Classification
2607.22725.paper_summary: Data augmentation is routinely used to improve generalization in image classification, but the assumptions underlying standard policies are poorly matched to coherent imaging. Laser speckle patterns are not generic textures; they arise from coherent interference, and their discriminative content is carried by structured stochastic spatial and frequency statistics. This study examines how controlled augmentation perturbations influence speckle-based material classification on the SensiCut dataset. We train ResNet18 and EfficientNet-B0 under a parametric augmentation framework comprising rotation, Gaussian blur, independent Gaussian noise, spatially correlated speckle-aware noise, intensity jitter, and spatial masking, and evaluate test performance using macro F1-score averaged over three random seeds. Separate ordinary least squares models link augmentation parameters to performance for each architecture. Across both models, Gaussian blur exerts a strong negative effect (p < 0.001), indicating that low-pass filtering suppresses high-frequency structure that is informative for material discrimination. Independent pixel-wise noise is likewise harmful (p = 0.003 for EfficientNet-B0 and p = 0.001 for ResNet18), consistent with disruption of local spatial coherence. In contrast, spatially correlated perturbations yield significant positive coefficients (p = 0.004 for EfficientNet-B0 and p = 0.001 for ResNet18), showing that variability can improve robustness when it preserves speckle organization. The fitted models explain a substantial fraction of performance variation (R2 = 0.796 for EfficientNet-B0 and R2 = 0.879 for ResNet18). These results show that, in laser speckle imaging, augmentation effectiveness is determined primarily by structural preservation rather than perturbation magnitude. The findings motivate physics-aware augmentation design for coherent optical sensing.
2607.22725.paper_summary_zh: 數據增強通常用於改善圖像分類的泛化能力，但標準政策背後的假設與相干成像不太匹配。激光散斑圖案並不是通用的紋理；它們源於相干干涉，其區分內容由結構化的隨機空間和頻率統計所攜帶。本研究考察了受控增強擾動如何影響基於散斑的材料分類，使用的是 SensiCut 數據集。我們在一個參數化增強框架下訓練 ResNet18 和 EfficientNet-B0，該框架包括旋轉、高斯模糊、獨立高斯噪聲、空間相關的散斑感知噪聲、強度抖動和空間遮罩，並使用三個隨機種子的宏觀 F1 分數來評估測試性能。分開的普通最小二乘模型將增強參數與每個架構的性能聯繫起來。在這兩個模型中，高斯模糊對性能產生強烈的負面影響（p < 0.001），這表明低通濾波抑制了對材料區分有信息的高頻結構。獨立的逐像素噪聲同樣有害（對 EfficientNet-B0 的 p = 0.003 和對 ResNet18 的 p = 0.001），這與局部空間相干性的破壞一致。相比之下，空間相關的擾動產生顯著的正係數（對 EfficientNet-B0 的 p = 0.004 和對 ResNet18 的 p = 0.001），顯示變異性在保持散斑組織的情況下可以提高穩健性。擬合模型解釋了性能變異的相當一部分（對 EfficientNet-B0 的 R2 = 0.796 和對 ResNet18 的 R2 = 0.879）。這些結果表明，在激光散斑成像中，增強的有效性主要由結構保留決定，而不是擾動的幅度。這些發現促使了對相干光學感測的物理感知增強設計。
